name: Millers Point and Dawes Point: Lower Fort St, Kent St, Argyle Place, High Lane, Windmill St, Trinity Ave

buildings.why: The heritage area's houses, most of them terraces of the 1830s-1880s, two or three storeys, rendered or of brick or sandstone, with pitched roofs of slate or iron (the listing's aerial photos of 55 Lower Fort St, 04, 06 and 21). The build gives no style in Millers Point (its buildings of no known use keep the CBD's look), so these had flat roofs and shopfronts. Anything taller, or flats, a warehouse or a church, keeps its own look.
